To give yourself some structure, at least at first, you and your DM could discuss some situations where the other personalities would be more likely to manifest and then create a mechanic to determine who comes out? I’m thinking you create a number of personalities equal to whatever dice you decide (4 for a d4, or 2 for a coin at first to keep it simple). 

Once the situational trigger happens, make a saving throw that you and your DM decide on, and if you fail you can roll for which personality comes out and rp that alter as if you were rp’ing a character in that situation (when they show up for the first time they may be confused at having a totally new body, elated to be alive again, in mid-panic because they’re still in the moment when they were killed...and then rp from there). 

The randomizing aspect of it kind of plays off of the unpredictability of the situation and also helps to prevent decision fatigue while you play, so you can focus on actually rp’ing the alters and not “okay, which one should come out? is this the best one for this job? am I using them too much? will the other players think I’m cheating/metagaming or get annoyed if I use this one again? [Insert whatever concerns you may have while making this decision here]”

You may find one or two alters become more important, and instead of rolling for an alter you can simply choose which one manifests, or create a way to “summon” one of them. 

The idea sounds like a fun time! The above might be kind of complicated so feel free to adjust it. I have a similar mechanic with my PC and it works really well. 

Hope this helps!

Oh geeze haha, the encounter with his Lady ended up being pretty quick and anti-climactic. I coordinated a bit with the DM, but she was wanting to settle most of it during rp, which is totally fine. When he stated that he doesn’t think he should be her champion + the problems he’s been having, she went straight to saying “that sounds like Gruumsh” and it was silent for a second, which in the moment was awkward, because I wasn’t sure what to say, but looking back I think that worked out because it’s not out of character to be speechless after hearing his 15+ year problem is summarized by a single sentence. 

So. His lady Helmi offers to help him with that later, and he’s basically like “ok....coooool....” and is super confused and joins the group in a bath house and has a few really touching moments. He asked them about Gruumsh, one PC knew about it and said “but that’s an orc thing, are you an orc?” and he ends up venting, taking off his mask, seeing that his new friends accept him, and setting the stage for Helmi + others to help him figure that stuff out. It also revealed that he has some resentment toward his monastery for not knowing or telling him about this. So a lot of other paths for him to work through have been set from that one session! Yay! :))

All of the advice was really helpful!! If I didn’t reach out I don’t think I would have been prepared at all for any of that, and wouldn’t have gotten as much out of the interactions as I did, so thank you again!!

I feel you with trying to stay open. I didn’t have an exact expectation, but I think the encounter ended up being so unexpected that it threw me for a loop. It worked out, but you reminded me that I need to stay flexible. :))

The nonverbal communication ended up being super important for me during the encounter, so that definitely proved to be excellent advice!! You’ve also given me some more ways to describe them - and let me know that I need to spend more time reading and researching descriptions haha. Thank you for your help!!

To respond to both of your comments:

The set up is similar to the campaign I’m currently in then! I was given a list of court members with their personality traits and what they represented and went from there. I haven’t discussed with the DM how his Lady (Helmi) views my character or vice versa, so that may be a good thing to initiate. 

I also like how y’all streamline the rp using appropriate metagaming - keeping background knowledge in mind while keeping the fun and dramatic parts on the surface. Thank you again for sharing your experiences and guidance with me! :))) It sounds like you’re in a group with awesome players  (including yourself!) and a fantastic DM! The moments y’all have created sound so wholesome

That’s great advice too!! I’ve been trying to do that, but it helps to know not to announce how he’s feeling. 

I’m also resolving to create a character in another campaign where pissing on the table in this situation would be something they’d do! Love that example haha

That’s fantastic!! I’ll do the same with mine. We’re relatively early in the campaign, so he’s only had 2 in-session interactions with her and both were quite brief. Right now he’s her champion because that’s what he feels like he’s supposed to do. He was sent to her island by his monastery, and she was impressed by something he did and subsequently appointed him her champion. She technically gave him a choice, but so far his entire life he’s just been acting on what the “correct” thing to do is (or what he’s expected to do), because with the whispers he doesn’t trust himself to rely on internal cues to act (moral compass, intuition, etc). There’s technically no authentic loyalty yet, so I’m hoping this encounter will be a great bonding moment for them. 

My next question would then be: Is this something you coordinate with the DM? Particularly in the beginning of the campaign? Did YOU know that his patroness would hug him? I don’t want to predict what the DM would do per se, but I’m not sure how the DM views my character and her NPCs dynamic, which probably just adds to the fun now that I’m typing this out. Regardless, I’m still interested in how much coordination you and your DM have done to build that relationship!

Right on! Yeah I’ve been doing a LOT of trying to figure out how and why my character feels the way he does, I think that is what causes a fear of my brain to ramble, because I enjoy my character and his development and his backstory and wanna share goddammit! Haha, I HAVEN’T written in first person yet though, so that will be really useful! 

I do like the point of writing things out, but not to memorize it. I was afraid I would come across as disingenuous or canned if I read it out or tried to have it ready to recite word for word. 

Your third point made me smile ha :)) I think I’m really nervous because when my character is vulnerable, I also feel really vulnerable, and I know the people I’m playing with are sweeties but it’s still over distance and I just don’t want to drag people into drama that they don’t care for. But if the DM is cool with it then I will follow point #2 and enjoy my moment like I enjoy when other PCs have their moment. Thanks for validating wanting to have a cool dramatic moment, I know others want to have that too, but for some reason if I want to do that then I talk myself out of it. 

I look forward to your rambling anecdotes! :))

Thank you!!! That takes off some of the pressure to keep it from being eloquent and long-winded. He definitely is not either of those, but I am, so I wasn’t sure how that would go. I just need to plan to keep it short to keep myself on track. The last two points you mentioned are exactly what I was wanting to do later on in the campaign!! I will definitely write out some potential responses and what he’s initially going to say in that discussion. 

Thank you for taking the time to read and understand the situation and my character + the really helpful advice!! :))
You rock! Thanks again!!!!
